{{Quote|Tell your people to take shelter. If you have warriors, now is the time.|Obi-Wan Kenobi, to Tion Medon, prior to the Battle of Utapau|<ref name="Revenge of the Sith">{{Film|III}}</ref>}}
'''Pau'ans''' were gaunt [[near-Human]]s native to the [[Planet/Legends|planet]] [[Utapau/Legends|Utapau]]. Also known as '''Utapauns''' and '''Ancients''' due to their long lifespans, they co-existed on Utapau with the [[Utai/Legends|Utai]]. The two [[Species/Legends|species]] got along well, with the lanky Pau'ans assuming leadership roles on the planet. Though some viewed the Pau'ans as frightening, they were friendly, and were more than happy to welcome visitors to their little-known world. Due to Utapau's remoteness in the [[Outer Rim Territories/Legends|Outer Rim Territories]], the Pau'ans were isolated for most of their history. However, they played a part in [[The galaxy/Legends|galactic]] events in [[19 BBY/Legends|19 BBY]], when the [[Confederacy of Independent Systems/Legends|Confederacy of Independent Systems]] conquered Utapau. The Pau'ans [[Battle of Utapau/Legends|opposed]] the Confederacy with the aid of the [[Galactic Republic/Legends|Republic]], and later opposed the [[Galactic Empire/Legends|Empire]], after Imperials took control of their planet following the [[Declaration of a New Order]].

==Biology and appearance==
[[File:Pauan_Jedi_Teacher_DoH.png|thumb|left|180px|A female Pau'an]]
The average member of the [[Sentience/Legends|sentient]] [[near-Human]] Pau'an, or Utapaun, as they were sometime called, [[Species/Legends|species]] stood taller than a [[Human/Legends|Human]], at approximately 1.9 [[Meter/Legends|meters]].<ref name="NEGAS" /> They were bald and their head was striped with furrowed [[Color/Legends|gray]] skin. Pau'ans weighed seventy [[Kilogram/Legends|kilograms]] on average.<ref name="Wizards.com article" /> Pau'ans had large, sunken [[Color/Legends|black]] [[Eye/Legends|eyes]] in red eye sockets and jagged, fang-like teeth used for tearing into raw meat, as they were [[Diet/Legends|carnivores]]. The species had pale, wrinkled skin, due to the fact that they lived in the [[Sinkhole/Legends|sinkholes]] of [[Utapau/Legends|Utapau]], giving them limited access to light. These traits caused some to view them as frightening. However, Pau'ans as a society were generally friendly, and were happy to welcome guests to their often overlooked [[Planet/Legends|world]].<ref name="NEGAS" /> Pau'ans had long lifespans, living up to 700 [[Time/Legends|years]], much longer than the [[Utai/Legends|Utai]], the other species native to Utapau.<ref name="Wizards.com article" /> This earned them the nickname of "Ancients". Members of the species were able to see well in darkness. Pau'ans had five fingers and toes, but were more mobile than they appeared. They often wore elaborate clothes intended to heighten their impressive stature.<ref name="NEGAS" /> Most Pau'ans spoke both [[Utapese/Legends|Utapese]] and [[Galactic Basic Standard/Legends|Basic]].<ref name="Wizards.com article" />

==Society and culture==
The Pau'ans fulfilled most of the governmental and administrative duties on Utapau, as the Utai did not desire such work, serving as laborers instead. Most Pau'ans served as leaders early in their lives, often managing teams of Utai laborers. This gave them experience that would be used later in their life. Pau'ans were kind leaders, and sympathetic to their subordinates.<ref name="Wizards.com article" /> Each city on Utapau was controlled by a [[Chairman of Utapau/Legends|Master of Port Administration]], a hereditary title reserved for Pau'ans. These administrators were assisted by advisory councils for making important decisions about their city, turning to the [[Utapauan Security Force]] when necessary. Each Administrator served on the [[Utapaun Committee/Legends|Utapauan Committee]] and oversaw planetary governance. However, the committee rarely made crucial decisions, as the cities were able to function on their own most of the time.<ref name="Wizards.com article" />

[[File:Pauan_and_Utai_DoH.png|thumb|right|200px|A Pau'an and two Utai]]
Despite the many differences between the Pau'ans and the Utai, the two species were able to co-exist peacefully, although inhabitants of the different Utapaun [[City/Legends|cities]] often had conflicts due to philosophical differences. Still, these conflicts rarely developed into [[Blood/Legends|bloodshed]], and it was more common for the cities to ignore each other. Each city had its own culture, and competition was fierce between the groups. However, they were able to cooperate when the situation necessitated it, such as during the [[Confederacy of Independent Systems/Legends|Confederate]] invasion of the planet in [[19 BBY/Legends|19 BBY]].<ref name="NEGAS" />

Pau'an society was a blend of a variety of styles and cultures, borne from the ancient merger with the Utai. Built into the sinkhole walls, Pau'an settlements such as the [[Pau City/Legends|Pau City]] [[Spaceport/Legends|spaceport]] were divided into different areas, each a mix of architectural styles and other-worldly design. They liked art, and enjoyed studying sculptures and finding ways to incorporate different artistic styles into their architecture. Pau'ans developed an industrial society, despite their seemingly primitive and natural image, though the Utai were the ones who actually did the hard work. The Utai did not mind, however, and collectively much preferred labor to positions of leadership.<ref name="NEGAS" /> They were able to power their city by wind, harnessing it through massive windmills. Over ninety-nine percent of the planet's power came from these windmills. Most Pau'ans rode living beasts like [[Varactyl/Legends|varactyls]] and [[Dactillion/Legends|dactillions]] instead of [[Speeder/Legends|speeders]].<ref name="Wizards.com article" /> Pau'ans, as well as Utai, were known for their love for [[Podracing/Legends|Podracing]].<ref name="Kinect">''[[Kinect Star Wars]]''</ref>

Pau'ans represented 30%&mdash;or approximately 28.5 million&mdash;of Utapau's total population of 90 million inhabitants.<ref name="EA">''[[The Essential Atlas]]'' states that there are 90 million inhabitants on Utapau, 30% of which are Pau'ans. Simple math was used from here to obtain a figure of 28.5 million.</ref>

==History==
{{Quote|Greetings, young Jedi. What brings you to our remote sanctuary?''"<br />"''Unfortunately, the war.''"<br />"''There is no war here, unless you've brought it with you.''"<br />"''With your kind permission, I should like some fuel and to use your city as a base as I search nearby systems for General Grievous.''"<br />"''He is here. We are being held hostage. They are watching us.|Tion Medon and Obi-Wan Kenobi|<ref name="Revenge of the Sith" />}}
[[File:PauanNEGAS.jpg|thumb|left|180px|A Pau'an]]
Pau'an civilization began around [[57,000 BBY/Legends|57,000 BBY]]. It was believed that settlers traveled to Utapau hoping to find a hospitable world to colonize after the destruction of their [[Homeworld/Legends|homeworld]]. Some created homes in the sinkholes, while others lived on the surface. Over time, the species changed genetically, becoming the Pau'ans and the Utai, two species with many differences but some similarities. Researchers from the [[University of Sanbra]] discovered evidence supporting the theory that the two species were related, although exact specifications were not certain.<ref name="Wizards.com article" /> Eventually, a climate change, causing severe winds, forced the Pau'ans underground, into the sinkholes. The Utai welcomed the Pau'ans, and over time, the two societies merged together to live in a mutually beneficial civilization. [[Timon Medon/Legends|Timon Medon]] was the Pau'an responsible for this, and he was held in high esteem by Pau'ans for his actions. Following the merging of the two cultures, they split into several different groups, forming sinkhole cities scattered across Utapau. [[Tion Medon/Legends|Tion Medon]], Port Administrator in [[19 BBY/Legends|19 BBY]], was named for Timon Medon. Pau'ans represented only about thirty percent of the population on Utapau, though as the administrators and bureaucrats of the sinkhole cities, their influence made up for their lack of numbers.<ref name="NEGAS" />

Due to trade restrictions placed on them by the [[Trade Federation/Legends|Trade Federation]], Pau'ans were unable to import many goods such as weapons or [[Starship/Legends|starships]], and were forced to create their own technology. As Utapau was located in the distant [[Outer Rim Territories/Legends|Outer Rim Territories]], few independent traders ventured to their planet; although many ventured there around [[49 BBY/Legends|49 BBY]] after hearing rumors that the [[Water/Legends|waters]] on the planet had miraculous healing properties. There were even claims that Utapau was the original home of the [[Jedi/Legends|Jedi]], although these reports were not new; they had originated millennia before. Though the Pau'ans did not want to draw attention to themselves for fear of meeting more powerful cultures who might try to conquer them, they eagerly welcomed visitors who wished to experience the healing for themselves. However, once the water was proven to be nothing more than ordinary water, most people forgot about Utapau, once again leaving it alone.<ref name="Wizards.com article" />

[[File:You_Can_End_This_DoH.png|thumb|right|250px|A Pau'an Force-user stands amidst a battle during the Galactic Civil War]]
The Pau'an culture was disturbed during the [[Clone Wars/Legends|Clone Wars]] by the [[Confederacy of Independent Systems/Legends|Confederacy of Independent Systems]]. Though the neutral Utapauns attempted to fight back with several [[Dreadnaught-class heavy cruiser/Legends|Rendili Star Dreadnaughts]], the CIS succeeded in conquering the planet as a stronghold.<ref name="Wizards.com article" /> Administrator Tion Medon and his aide [[Lampay Fay/Legends|Lampay Fay]] were forced to host [[General/Legends|General]] [[Grievous/Legends|Grievous]] and his allies on Utapau, turning the planet into a Separatist safehouse.<ref name="Reversal">''[[Reversal of Fortune]]''</ref> The Pau'ans hid their [[Starfighter/Legends|starfighters]], [[Porax-38 starfighter|Porax-38 fighters]], so they would not be used by the Separatist war machine or destroyed.<ref name="Starfighter article">''{{Wizards|url=default.asp?x=starwars/article/SBPreview6|text=''Starship Battles'' Preview 6}}''</ref>

With the arrival of [[Jedi Master/Legends|Jedi Master]] [[Obi-Wan Kenobi/Legends|Obi-Wan Kenobi]], many Pau'ans and Utai [[Battle of Utapau/Legends|fought back]] against the [[Droid/Legends|droid]] forces, with the Utai flying their starfighters in an effort to help liberate their planet,<ref name="Revenge of the Sith" /> though Utapau was subjugated once more with the formation of the [[Galactic Empire/Legends|Galactic Empire]].<ref name="NEGAS" /> The Empire used the planet's resources with no thought to the native cultures that were affected, and Pau'an captives were shipped as [[Slavery/Legends|slaves]] for several Imperial projects, including the colonization of [[Byss/Legends|Byss]].<ref name="Recruitment">''[[Evasive Action: Recruitment]]''</ref> Some Pau'ans and Utai created resistance movements, and the different cities were able to unify once more in the face of a great threat.<ref name="Wizards.com article" />

Following the liberation of their planet by the [[New Republic/Legends|New Republic]], they joined the new galactic government, hoping to avoid further enslavement and poor treatment at the hands of the leaders of the galaxy.<ref name="NEGAS" />Following the [[Yuuzhan Vong War]], the Utapauan Committee elected to join the [[Galactic Federation of Free Alliances|Galactic Alliance]], holding democracy as vital to the preservation of the galaxy. When the [[Sith Lord/Legends|Sith Lord]] [[Darth Krayt]] took control of the [[Darth Krayt's Galactic Empire|Galactic Empire]], Utapau sheltered [[Admiral/Legends|Admiral]] [[Gar Stazi]] of the [[Galactic Alliance Remnant]] late in the [[Second Imperial Civil War|war]] after having providing the [[Galactic Alliance Defense Fleet|GA fleet]] shelter throughout the conflict.<ref name="EP2">[[Legacy (2006) 49|''Legacy'' (2006) 49]]</ref>

Condemning the [[Genocide on Dac|genocide]] wrought by the [[One Sith|Sith]] on [[Dac/Legends|Dac]], Port Administrator [[Telan Medon]] of [[Pau City/Legends|Pau City]] agreed to harbor Stazi and his wounded men deep in the labyrinthine caves that pocketed the capital. Unbeknownst to the Pau'ans, Sith scientist [[Vul Isen]] had established a [[Vul Isen's laboratory (Utapau)|laboratory]] on the planet, conducting illegal experiments on the natives. Located within plain sight in one of Pau City's main precincts, the lab's function was to provide Isen a space to concoct a deadly virus that would wipe all life from Utapau indefinitely. Before Isen could unleash the deadly plague, [[Jedi Knight/Legends|Jedi Knight]] [[Cade Skywalker]] infiltrated the lab and cut Isen down, securing the toxin and saving the Pau'an race from extinction.<ref name="EP2" />

==Pau'ans in the galaxy==
[[File:DarthDesolousface.png|thumb|left|250px|Darth Desolous, a Pau'an Sith]]
Pau'ans were rarely found on a world other than Utapau, owing mainly to the remoteness of their planet. However, one individual who did achieve notoriety was the Pau'an [[Darth Desolous]], who served as a Jedi prior to his fall to the [[Dark side of the Force/Legends|dark side]], when he became a [[Sith/Legends|Sith]]. Born in approximately [[3522 BBY]], Desolous joined the [[Jedi Order/Legends|Jedi Order]] before being expelled due to his violent tendencies. He turned to the dark side, returned to Utapau, and trained a number of Pau'ans in melee combat. Desolous and his army [[Death/Legends|killed]] a number of Jedi before he was defeated and killed by the [[Jedi High Council/Legends|Jedi High Council]] at [[Yaga Minor/Legends|Yaga Minor]].<ref name="The Force Unleashed">''[[Star Wars: The Force Unleashed]]''</ref> In another instance, [[Lar Le'Ung]] attained the rank of Master within the [[New Jedi Order|rebuilt Jedi Order]] by [[25 ABY/Legends|25 ABY]], only to die at the beginning of the bloody [[Yuuzhan Vong War]].<ref name="Invasion 2">[[Invasion 2|''Invasion'' 2]]</ref>

Pau'ans that left Utapau could be found as aides to nobles and [[Senator/Legends|senators]]. Having Pau'an aides was seen as a status symbol, much like having [[Caamasi/Legends|Caamasi]] advisors. As the Pau'ans were skilled leaders, some were recruited by the [[Corporate Sector Authority/Legends|Corporate Sector Authority]] to work as managers of corporations. At one point, so many Pau'ans were recruited by companies that the CSA had to intervene and force businesses to take only a limited number of Pau'ans to be managers. However, following the rise of the Empire, Pau'ans were mistreated, and the assistants who had formerly enjoyed pleasant, successful lives were mocked and used as slaves. Imperial nobles used Pau'ans as servants and pets<ref name="Wizards.com article" /> while female members of the species were used as their concubines.<ref name="TFU2vg">''[[Star Wars: The Force Unleashed II]]''</ref>

At least [[Unidentified Pau'an interrogator|one Pau'an]] joined the Galactic Empire, serving as an interrogator. This particular Pau'an enjoyed [[Torture/Legends|torturing]] suspects, and would use torture to force them to divulge information. Around [[0 ABY/Legends|0 ABY]], he interrogated [[Princess/Legends|Princess]] [[Leia Organa Solo/Legends|Leia Organa]], a member of the [[Alliance to Restore the Republic/Legends|Rebel Alliance]], in an effort to determine the identity of the [[Luke Skywalker/Legends|pilot]] who had [[Battle of Yavin/Legends|destroyed]] the Empire's [[DS-1 Orbital Battle Station/Legends|Death Star]] [[Superweapon/Legends|superweapon]]. This individual was killed by the [[Assassin/Legends|assassin]] [[X-7]] before he could force any information from Organa.<ref name="Rebel Force: Hostage">''[[Rebel Force: Hostage]]''</ref>

==Behind the scenes==
The Pau'ans were created for [[Star Wars: Episode III Revenge of the Sith|''Star Wars'': Episode III ''Revenge of the Sith'']], although Utapau was the name of [[Tatooine/Legends|Tatooine]] in the [[The Star Wars rough draft|rough]], [[Adventures of the Starkiller, Episode I: The Star Wars|second]], and [[The Star Wars: From The Adventures of Luke Starkiller|third]] drafts of [[Star Wars: Episode IV A New Hope|''A New Hope'']].<ref name="Making">''[[The Making of Star Wars: The Definitive Story Behind the Original Film]]''</ref> Utapau was also the name of [[Naboo/Legends|Naboo]] in the [[Star Wars: Episode I The Beginning|first draft]] of [[Star Wars: Episode I The Phantom Menace|''The Phantom Menace'']].<ref name="Utapau">{{DB|location|utapau|Utapau}}</ref> The Pau'un species first appeared in the [[Star Wars Legends|''Star Wars'' Legends]] continuity in the [[Star Wars: Revenge of the Sith (novelization)|''Revenge of the Sith'' novelization]] and the [[Star Wars: Episode III — Revenge of the Sith 2|second issue]] of the [[Star Wars: Episode III — Revenge of the Sith (comic series)|''Revenge of the Sith'' comic adaptation]].

The design of the Pau'ans for ''Revenge of the Sith'' was originally intended for the [[Mustafarian/Legends|natives]] of [[Mustafar/Legends|Mustafar]]. They were designed as [[Wikipedia:lemur|lemur]]-like creatures per [[George Lucas]].<ref name="Databank">{{DB|species|utapaun|Utapaun}}</ref> Artist [[Sang Jun Lee]] drew some initial sketches of the Pau'an species, and [[Robert E. Barnes]] and [[Michael Murnane|Mike Murnane]] created sculptures of their faces. The design developed over time and was later changed to the Pau'ans' current appearance as ''Revenge of the Sith'' developed.<ref name="Aliens">{{InsiderCite|90|Aliens of Episode III}}</ref> Their backstory was later expanded on in ''[[The New Essential Guide to Alien Species]]'', and [http://wizards.com/default.asp?x=starwars/article/sagaenhancementpauans an article] on [[Wizards.com]]. The Pau'ans in ''Revenge of the Sith'' were created through a mix of prosthetic makeup effects and [[Wiki:Computer-generated imagery|computer-generated imagery]].<ref name="Databank" /> The design of their face was inspired by an African tribal mask.<ref name="Star Wars.com article">{{SWArchive|url=episode-iii/bts/profile/f20050623/index.html|text=Alien Sophistication: Bruce Spence as Tion Medon}}</ref>
